newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China 1996 gold output 115T - China Gold Corp pres.
newsitem.headline: China 1996 gold output 115T - China Gold Corp pres.

text.p: China's 1996 gold production will hit 115 tonnes, against 108 tonnes in 1995, the president of the China National Gold Corp, Cui Xiwu, said on Monday.
Cui, also deputy director of the Gold Bureau of the Ministry of Metallurgical Industry, told Reuters in Hong Kong that China's gold production for 1996 could be higher than 115 tonnes.

Cui said the ministry (MMI) is discussing liberalising gold prices with the People's Bank of China and the State Council (cabinet), but he said it was difficult to predict when gold prices in China would be freed.
Cui is in Hong Kong attending the three-day Asia Gold Congress.
The Chinese government currently regulates that all gold produced in China must be sold to the central bank at a set price.
China has 900 gold mines, Cui said, the major being in Shandong, Henan, Shaanxi, Heilongjiang, Liaoning, Inner Mongolia and Jilin provinces.
Some 2,000 tonnes of new reserves have been discovered, he said, though did not elaborate on where or when.
